precepts.text: The Pharisees challenged Christ's disciples for plucking the ears of corn on the sabbath day, saying it was not lawful.
precepts.point: Link this history with the words of Christ: when the Pharisees challenged his disciples for plucking the ears of corn on the sabbath day, Christ recounted this very history of David and the shewbread. Precept this in your bibles if you do not have it already.

precepts.why:
Christ “went through the corn fields on the sabbath day; and his disciples began, as they went, to pluck the ears of corn. And the Pharisees said unto him, Behold, why do they on the sabbath day that which is not lawful?”

When the Pharisees challenged his disciples, Christ recounted this very history of David and the shewbread. Link this history with the words of Christ, and precept it in your bibles if you do not have it already.

precepts.why:
Christ answered, “Have ye never read what David did, when he had need, and was an hungred, he, and they that were with him? How he went into the house of God in the days of Abiathar the high priest, and did eat the shewbread, which is not lawful to eat but for the priests, and gave also to them which were with him?”

This is that history. In Nob, “the priest gave him hallowed bread: for there was no bread there but the shewbread, that was taken from before the Lord.” David had been out in the field three days, fearful of king Saul, when he came to Nob in need.

note.label: 1 Samuel 21: The Hallowed Bread and the Feigned Madness

points: David fled that day for fear of Saul and went to Achish the king of Gath, and the servants of Achish knew him by the song, Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands.

note.label: 1 Samuel 21: The Hallowed Bread and the Feigned Madness

points: David laid up these words in his heart and was sore afraid of Achish, so he changed his behaviour and feigned himself mad, scrabbling on the doors of the gate and letting his spittle fall down upon his beard. David was playing crazy; he was fearful, and Achish dismissed him as a mad man.

note.label: 1 Samuel 21: The Hallowed Bread and the Feigned Madness

points: Read on into the next chapter: David came to the priest, and the priest was afraid at the meeting of David: “Why art thou alone, and no man with thee?” Remember, a couple of days ago you had the new moon feast, the day that, by their doctrine, determines the Sabbath.

David told the priest, “The king hath commanded me a business”: I’m commanded by Saul to come here and grab some food from you. David is starving; he’s been hiding all this time, so he wants to eat. “Give me five loaves of bread in mine hand, or what there is present”: what you got to give me for food?

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

points: “There is no common bread under mine hand”: I don’t have regular bread here, common bread is not here. Watch this: “but there is hallowed bread.” When is hallowed bread made? On the Sabbath.

Three days ago you had a new moon, and in their doctrine the new moon is what sets the 7-day Sabbath. Now you have another 7-day Sabbath, and the priest baked the bread on that Sabbath. This isn’t a week later; it’s the same time. “If the young men have kept themselves at least from women”: if you guys are clean, you can eat the holy bread.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

points: “Of a truth women have been kept from us about these three days.” These three days, not seven. This is the third day: the new moon was the first day, the second day David’s place was empty, and here he arrives the third day, and he is offered holy bread that was made on the Sabbath day. That means the new moon does not determine the seven day Sabbaths. Everyone got it?

They will try to be sick and say no, that’s three days more: the two days of chapter 20 and then three more. Two plus three is five; that ain’t seven days, that’s not a week. Why you making shewbread on the fifth day? It’s seventh day bread. If it was seven days later, you don’t make shewbread on the fifth day of the week. Either way you count it, there’s no argument here: the new moon does not determine a 7-day Sabbath. It makes no sense.

“And the bread is in a manner common”: it’s common because you guys are clean; since you’re clean, the bread is common to you now, “yea, though it were sanctified this day in the vessel.” Sanctified this day in the vessel means it was baked that day in the vessel.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

points: “So the priest gave him hallowed bread: for there was no bread there but the shewbread, that was taken from before the Lord, to put hot bread in the day when it was taken away.” He gave him the shewbread made on the Sabbath. To put hot bread there the day it was taken away: the day David took it, it was hot and fresh bread, like Little Caesar pizza, pizza, hot and ready. That’s what it means.

So you cannot use the new moon as a 7-day Sabbath. Three days later another 7-day Sabbath popped up? That don’t make sense. And if you argue chapter 20 is two days and chapter 21 is three days, that gives you five, and you still can’t get a seven day Sabbath out of five days. There’s no way around it: either you’re miscounting on purpose or you’re not reading it properly, one or the other. Every corner is being covered.
